title: 52yo F Russell's Viper Envenomation
chiefComplaint: Snakebite to the right foot while harvesting, now bleeding from the gums
background: Bitten two hours ago while cutting rice at dusk. A neighbour tied a cloth tourniquet above the knee and applied crushed herbs to the wound. She describes a short, thick, brown snake with dark oval blotches. She has taken no medication. She lives 40 km from the hospital and the pickup truck broke down on the way. Four vials of Russell's viper antivenom are in the fridge and the next delivery is Tuesday.

exam.finding: Anxious, in severe pain, cooperative and fully alert, a cloth tourniquet still tied tightly around the right thigh
Spontaneous gum bleeding, blood-stained saliva, no ptosis, no ophthalmoplegia, full mouth opening, normal voice. Absence of neurotoxic signs helps distinguish from cobra or krait envenomation
Sinus tachycardia, borderline hypotension, capillary refill 3 seconds, dorsalis pedis pulse present on the bitten limb
Clear breath sounds, normal effort, no respiratory muscle weakness, single breath count 32
Soft, mild generalised tenderness, no guarding, no flank bruising, bowel sounds present

Two fang marks 12 mm apart on the dorsum of the right foot with oozing serosanguinous fluid, swelling to mid-calf, herbal paste over the wound, bruising extending proximally, bleeding from the IV cannula site
GCS 15, no ptosis, no bulbar weakness, normal power in all limbs, sensation intact distally

investigations.name: 20 minute whole blood clotting test
investigations.report: Fresh venous blood placed in a clean, dry, unwashed glass tube fails to clot at 20 minutes. This is the single most useful test in a Thai district hospital and it is the indication for antivenom on its own.

investigations.name: INR and fibrinogen
investigations.report: Venom induced consumption coagulopathy. Fresh frozen plasma without antivenom is fuel on a fire, the venom will consume it too.

investigations.name: Platelet count
investigations.report: Thrombocytopenia, characteristic of Russell's viper envenomation.

investigations.name: Creatinine and potassium
investigations.report: Early acute kidney injury. Russell's viper is the leading snake cause of dialysis-requiring renal failure in Southeast Asia.

investigations.name: Urinalysis
investigations.value: Blood 3+, protein 2+, no red cells on microscopy
investigations.report: Positive dipstick blood with no red cells indicates myoglobinuria or haemoglobinuria.

data.label: Remove the tourniquet carefully and immobilise the limb
actions: Slow removal of the constricting band with monitoring
Splint the limb at heart level
Remove the herbal paste and clean the wound
Do not incise, suck or apply ice

doseMap.Slow removal of the constricting band wi: Release with resuscitation drugs at hand. Sudden release can wash a bolus of venom into the circulation

data.label: 20 minute whole blood clotting test and species identification
actions: Examine for neurotoxic signs: ptosis, single breath count

data.label: Give specific antivenom for systemic envenomation
actions: Adrenaline drawn up at the bedside before infusion

doseMap.Russell's viper monovalent antivenom IV: 3 vials reconstituted in 100 mL normal saline over 30-60 min. Repeat after 6 hours if the clotting test remains non-clotting
doseMap.Adrenaline drawn up at the bedside befor: 0.5 mg 1:1000 IM ready for anaphylactoid reaction, which occurs in up to 20% of infusions

data.label: Anaphylactoid reaction during infusion
data.narrative: Twelve minutes in she develops urticaria, wheeze and a fall in blood pressure. The infusion is stopped, IM adrenaline is given, and after 20 minutes the antivenom is restarted at a slower rate and completed. This is expected, not a reason to withhold the only effective treatment.

data.label: Do not shame the family for the tourniquet and the herbs (Empathy)
data.narrative: The neighbour who tied the tourniquet is standing in the corridor waiting to be blamed. You tell him plainly that the cloth and the paste do not help and can cause harm, and in the same breath that driving her 40 km on a broken truck is why she is alive. He listens to the first part because you said the second. He is the village health volunteer for four hundred people, and next time he will bring the next patient straight in.

data.label: Repeat clotting test at 6 hours and give further antivenom if still non-clotting
actions: Repeat 20 minute whole blood clotting test at 6 hours
Do not give FFP or platelets before antivenom

doseMap.Further antivenom if non-clotting: 3 more vials. Only two vials remain in the fridge, so contact the regional depot and the referral hospital now, not at 06:00

data.label: Fluids and monitoring for acute kidney injury
actions: IV crystalloid targeting urine output 1-2 mL/kg/h
Hourly urine output and daily creatinine

doseMap.Tetanus prophylaxis: Give once the coagulopathy has corrected, not into a bleeding muscle

data.label: Coagulopathy corrected
data.narrative: Clotting restored at 14 hours after a total of 6 vials. Gum bleeding stops. Creatinine peaks at 3.4 mg/dL on day 3 and she requires two sessions of haemodialysis, then recovers.

data.label: Disposition
data.narrative: Discharged on day 9 with normal renal function and a permanently swollen foot. The limb was never fasciotomised, which was correct: swelling from envenomation is rarely true compartment syndrome and fasciotomy into a coagulopathic limb is a well documented way to kill someone.
